learningObjective: Identify legitimate motivations for loop fission and cases where fission is counter-productive.
stem: Loop fission (loop distribution) splits one loop body into two loops with the same iteration space. Which of the following are legitimate motivations for loop fission in a numerical / tensor pipeline? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: To relieve register pressure when a single loop body has too many simultaneously live scalars, at the cost of touching some intermediate arrays twice.
To allow vectorization or parallelization of a subset of statements whose dependence structure permits it, while leaving unvectorizable statements in a separate loop.
To enable different tile sizes or schedules for the two halves, e.g., a compute-bound half and a memory-bound half.
To improve cache behavior in a producer-consumer chain where a single loop body already fits in L1 cache and the intermediate values are reused within the same iteration.
To convert a semantically incorrect program into a correct one by re-ordering side-effecting operations.

explanation: Loop fission is the inverse of fusion. Legitimate uses: (A) split a register-heavy body so each half fits in the register budget without spills; (B) isolate vectorizable statements from unvectorizable ones so the vectorizer can act on one half; (C) allow independent scheduling / tiling for the two halves. (D) is the opposite of the fission use case: if a single body already fits in cache and reuses intermediates, fusion is preferred; fission would force materialization of the intermediates. (E) is wrong: fission is a semantics-preserving transformation only when the dependence graph permits it — it cannot fix bugs, only preserve behavior.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: canonical register-pressure motivation for fission.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: describes a case where fusion is preferred; fission would hurt cache behavior.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: fission requires legality; it cannot 'fix' semantics by reordering side effects.

assumptions: Both halves of the fission preserve the dependence graph (no forward-crossing dependences created).
nonImplications: Does not imply that any of these motivations always yield a net speedup; each is a candidate transformation that must be validated.

distractorRationales.E: Attributes semantic-fixing power to a semantics-preserving transformation.
